title: Read a labelled choroid-plexus field

regions.label: Epithelial covering
regions.observation: A peripheral row of purple nuclei follows the outside of the rounded profile.
regions.interpretation: This is the epithelial covering of a vascular frond; the outer surface faces ventricular CSF in the supplied context.
regions.limit: The field does not resolve individual tight-junction strands or every cell border.

regions.label: Stromal core
regions.observation: Pale pink tissue lies inside the epithelial covering and around an internal vessel.
regions.interpretation: The core separates vascular endothelium from the outer epithelial blood–CSF interface.
regions.limit: Do not assign every stromal nucleus a specific cell identity from this H&E field.

regions.label: Erythrocyte-containing vessel
regions.observation: Strongly pink-red erythrocytes occupy an internal lumen.
regions.interpretation: This is a vascular space within the frond, not a secretory lumen bounded by the outer epithelium.
regions.limit: Endothelial fenestrations and transport rates cannot be read directly at this resolution.

model: I see repeated epithelial-covered profiles with pale stromal cores and erythrocyte-containing vascular lumina. The provider identifies human lateral-ventricle choroid plexus. The epithelial apical surface faces ventricular CSF, while its basal surface faces the core. Blood reaching that core still encounters the epithelial blood–CSF interface. H&E supports the architecture but does not directly resolve tight-junction strands, fenestrations or transporter function. Permanent labels make this a guided field; age, disease status and detailed preparation are not supplied.
